outcome.substitution: MOZAK keeps a capped deterministic linked-Scope summary in project context and exposes the complete relationship inventory through a separate bounded detail command with explicit count and truncation metadata.

outcome.rationale: MOZAK makes no transfer claim from the source paper benchmarks. Acceptance depends only on MOZAK-specific live CLI observations and project tests.

target_evidence.observation: The configured KB remains authoritative, hash-pinned, and fail-closed; project context reports linked records as advisory, unaccepted, and non-trust-transferring.
Scope manifests hold content and typed relationships while project_registry.rs controls the CLI exposure layer independently.
The target design replaces unbounded inline expansion with a fixed inline cap plus a bounded complete detail path.
The live Potjera project context emitted 17 relationship-specific records inline, demonstrating context growth on the owner-configured KB.
The proposed edit is attributed to tool_behavior because authoritative Scope content and relationship schema remain unchanged.
The baseline defines fixed project inputs and explicit acceptance checks for inline bounds, completeness, safety, ordering, and drift behavior.
MOZAK stores evaluation and comparison artifacts under .mozak so rejected or inconclusive changes remain reviewable.
Project refresh, planning acceptance, execution, release, and Concept adoption remain separate owner-controlled gates.
